entities.summary:
Akbar Al Baker, a prominent Qatari businessman and former CEO of Qatar Airways from 1997 until October 2023, stands as a pivotal figure in the transformation of global aviation and Qatar's emergence as a major international hub. His tenure at the helm of the state-owned airline coincided with Qatar's ambitious economic diversification strategy, leveraging its vast hydrocarbon wealth to build world-class infrastructure and services. Beyond aviation, Al Baker also chaired Qatar Tourism until late 2023, playing a crucial role in shaping the nation's international image and visitor economy, embodying the state-driven development model characteristic of many Gulf economies in the early 21st century.

Under Al Baker's leadership, Qatar Airways expanded from a small regional carrier to a global powerhouse, operating a vast network of over 160 destinations across six continents with a modern fleet exceeding 250 aircraft. Key achievements include the airline's entry into the Oneworld airline alliance in 2013, significantly broadening its global reach and competitive standing. He also oversaw the development and 2014 opening of Hamad International Airport in Doha, a multi-billion dollar facility designed to serve as a primary gateway between East and West, consistently ranked among the world's best airports. This period saw aggressive expansion into new markets, often challenging established legacy carriers and reshaping competitive dynamics in the airline industry.
